title: Jharkhand Weather Update: लौटते मॉनसून ने बदला मौसम, चार दिन बारिश के आसार - 22Scope
article_text:
झारखंड में लौटते मॉनसून और साइक्लोनिक ट्रफ के असर से मौसम बदला। रांची, कांके, जमशेदपुर समेत कई जिलों में बारिश हुई, अगले चार दिन भी बारिश के आसार हैं।

Jharkhand Weather Update रांची: लौटते मॉनसून और साइक्लोनिक ट्रफ के प्रभाव से झारखंड के मौसम ने मंगलवार को अचानक करवट ली। राज्य के कई हिस्सों में बारिश हुई, जबकि रांची से सटे कांके में मेघ गर्जन के साथ ओलावृष्टि भी हुई। बारिश के कारण तापमान में गिरावट दर्ज की गयी और मौसम सुहाना हो गया।

नक्शे देखें

Jharkhand Weather Update:कांके में ओलावृष्टि के साथ 41 मिमी बारिश

मंगलवार को कांके में सबसे अधिक बारिश दर्ज की गयी। यहां मेघ गर्जन और ओलावृष्टि के साथ 41 मिमी बारिश हुई। रांची शहर में नौ मिमी बारिश दर्ज की गयी। इसके अलावा जमशेदपुर में 26.2 मिमी, हजारीबाग में 28 मिमी, लातेहार में सात मिमी, लोहरदगा में पांच मिमी और सिमडेगा में 16 मिमी बारिश हुई।

बारिश के साथ कई इलाकों में बादल छाये रहे। अचानक बदले मौसम के कारण लोगों को गर्मी से राहत मिली। मौसम विभाग के अनुसार, राज्य में मौसम में बदलाव का प्रमुख कारण लौटता मॉनसून और साइक्लोनिक ट्रफ का प्रभाव है।

Key Highlights

कांके में मेघ गर्जन और ओलावृष्टि के साथ 41 मिमी बारिश

रांची शहर में नौ मिमी बारिश दर्ज

जमशेदपुर में 26.2 मिमी और हजारीबाग में 28 मिमी बारिश

सात और आठ अक्तूबर को कई हिस्सों में बारिश के आसार

नौ और 10 अक्तूबर को भी बादल और हल्की बारिश की संभावना

Jharkhand Weather Update:सात और आठ अक्तूबर को भी बारिश के आसार

मौसम विज्ञान केंद्र के अनुसार सात और आठ अक्तूबर को झारखंड के कई हिस्सों में आकाश में बादल छाये रह सकते हैं। इस दौरान मेघ गर्जन के साथ कहीं-कहीं हल्की से मध्यम दर्जे की बारिश होने की संभावना है।

मौसम विभाग के पूर्वानुमान के अनुसार, अगले दो दिनों में राज्य के अलग-अलग हिस्सों में मौसम का मिजाज बदला हुआ रह सकता है। कुछ स्थानों पर गरज के साथ बारिश होने की स्थिति बन सकती है।

Jharkhand Weather Update:नौ और 10 अक्तूबर को भी छाये रहेंगे बादल

नौ और 10 अक्तूबर को भी झारखंड में आकाश में बादल छाये रहने की संभावना है। इस दौरान मेघ गर्जन के साथ हल्की बारिश हो सकती है। मौसम विभाग ने लोगों को मौसम में होने वाले बदलाव पर नजर रखने की सलाह दी है।

लौटते मॉनसून के असर से आने वाले दिनों में राज्य के अलग-अलग हिस्सों में बारिश की गतिविधियां देखने को मिल सकती हैं। रांची समेत कई जिलों में बादल और बारिश का दौर जारी रहने की संभावना है।

title: NDMA Begins Mon District Monsoon Damage Assessment - Urban Acres
article_text:
A central post-disaster needs assessment team from the National Disaster Management Authority has begun assessing monsoon damage in Nagaland’s Mon district, asking government departments to document losses accurately before recovery requirements are compiled.

The NDMA team visited Mon district on Tuesday as part of a wider post-disaster needs assessment being conducted across Nagaland. During the visit, it met the district administration and representatives of various line departments at the conference hall of the Mon deputy commissioner.

Mon Deputy Commissioner Wennyei Konyak briefed the team on the extent of damage reported in the district. Officials from the departments responsible for different public services and infrastructure also presented details of monsoon-related damage and submitted reports to the central team.

The assessment is significant because the documentation prepared at the district level will form the basis for identifying recovery requirements. The NDMA team asked the departments to record and report all actual damage, with the stated aim of ensuring that the assessment reflects the losses on the ground.

The report supplied to the Times of India did not specify the number of damaged structures, roads, bridges, public facilities or households in Mon district. It also did not provide an estimate of the financial loss or announce any recovery package, funding allocation or implementation timeline. Those details are expected to depend on the completion of departmental reports and the wider assessment process.

The district-level meeting places the administration’s immediate task beyond recording individual incidents. Officials from multiple line departments are required to compile information on the effects of the monsoon within their respective areas and submit it for consolidation. This creates a common evidence base for the state and central authorities to determine the scale of post-disaster needs.

The exercise also shows how disaster recovery begins with administrative verification. Damage reported locally must be documented, checked and consolidated before the requirements for restoration and recovery can be assessed at the state and national levels. In Mon, the NDMA team’s instruction to report actual damage makes the quality and completeness of departmental records a central part of the process.

The visit forms part of the assessment being conducted across Nagaland, rather than a standalone review limited to Mon district. The supplied report does not state when the state-wide assessment will conclude or identify the next stage after the district meetings. Further decisions on recovery needs will follow the completion and evaluation of the damage reports submitted by the line departments.

title: Central team assesses flood damage in Arunachal; satellite imagery to aid loss assessment - DD News
article_text:
An Inter-Ministerial Central Team (IMCT), led by Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) Joint Secretary Nishtha Tiwari, visited flood-affected areas of Arunachal Pradesh to assess the damage caused by recent flash floods and landslides. The team assured the State of all possible assistance from the Centre even as several areas remained inaccessible due to continuing rainfall.

The eight-member delegation inspected affected areas, including Lower Siang district, to assess the extent of the damage. However, adverse weather conditions and blocked roads prevented the team from reaching some of the worst-hit locations.

Speaking during the visit, Tiwari said satellite imagery had been shared with the State administration to assist in assessing losses in areas that remain inaccessible.

“Satellite images have been received, and a report based on them has been shared with the State administration to assist you with your loss assessment. Please utilise this report for areas that are currently inaccessible. A team led by the Ministry of Home Affairs has arrived from New Delhi to assess the damage and the disaster caused by the recent heavy rains and flash floods in Arunachal Pradesh. Since it is still raining and many areas remain inaccessible—preventing team visits and making helicopter operations impossible in this weather—the team is covering as much ground as possible. The tour is currently ongoing and has not yet concluded. Today, we attempted to reach Lower Siang, but the route was impassable, so we are continuing with our duties. The tour is still in progress,” she said.

BJP MLA Tojir Kadu welcomed the Centre’s response and said the visiting team had witnessed the scale of destruction, although several severely affected areas remained beyond reach.

“A Central Team led by a Joint Secretary from the Ministry of Home Affairs, this inter-departmental ministerial team inspected the affected areas. We are satisfied with the prompt action taken by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in dispatching this team. Senior officers have also visited today to assess the situation of our people. They have seen the extent of the damage here, though some areas that suffered severe devastation—specifically within certain circles—remain inaccessible. Consequently, the Central Team could not reach those specific locations, though they have gauged the distance and the scale of the damage. The damage is so extensive that it is difficult to estimate the financial cost right now,” Kadu said.

Deputy Commissioner of East Siang, Sonalika Jiwani, said the district administration had completed its preliminary assessment and was working to strengthen its reports to secure adequate assistance.

“We have already completed an assessment and are seeking guidance on how to refine our reports to secure the best possible assistance. We are confident that if we present the case properly, our people and we will quickly receive adequate compensation for our infrastructure and relief needs. Koyu is a subdivision falling under the Lower Siang district. They are cut off; three of our villages in the Kora Circle of East Siang district are cut off,” she said.

Meanwhile, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an orange warning for Arunachal Pradesh for July 10, forecasting very heavy rainfall accompanied by thunderstorms, lightning and squally winds.

The central team’s assessment is continuing, with several affected areas remaining inaccessible due to persistent rainfall.

-ANI

Haryana Weather Update: अगले 48 घंटे बहुत भारी, हरियाणा में तूफानी बारिश का अलर्ट, 50 कि.मी. की रफ्तार से चलेंगी हवाएं, जानें हाल
हरियाणा में मौसम ने बदली करवट, 12 अक्टूबर तक बारिश का अलर्ट; मंडियों में भीगा धान
Published On Oct 07, 2026 11:34 AM IST

Haryana Weather Update: हिसार, संदीप सिंहमार। हरियाणा में मौसम ने एक बार फिर करवट ले ली है। मंगलवार शाम से प्रदेश में पश्चिमी विक्षोभ सक्रिय हो गया है। इसके प्रभाव से अगले पांच दिनों तक कई इलाकों में रुक-रुककर बारिश होने की संभावना है। मौसम विभाग ने बुधवार को प्रदेश के 9 जिलों में यलो अलर्ट जारी किया है।

अंबाला, पंचकूला, यमुनानगर, करनाल, कुरुक्षेत्र, पानीपत, सोनीपत, गुरुग्राम और फरीदाबाद में गरज-चमक के साथ हल्की से मध्यम बारिश होने का अनुमान है। इस दौरान तेज हवाएं भी चल सकती हैं।

50 किलोमीटर प्रति घंटे की रफ्तार से चलेंगी हवाएं

मौसम विभाग के अनुसार अलर्ट वाले जिलों में 40 से 50 किलोमीटर प्रति घंटे की रफ्तार से तेज हवाएं चलने की संभावना है। कई स्थानों पर बिजली चमकने और गरज के साथ बारिश हो सकती है।

मौसम खराब रहने के दौरान लोगों को सावधानी बरतने की सलाह दी गई है। खुले स्थानों पर रहने वाले लोगों को विशेष सतर्कता बरतने और तेज आंधी-तूफान के दौरान सुरक्षित स्थान पर रहने की सलाह दी गई है।

पंचकूला में रात को गिरे ओले

मंगलवार रात पंचकूला में मौसम ने अचानक करवट ली। यहां गरज-चमक के साथ ओले भी गिरे। वहीं पानीपत और सोनीपत में तेज हवाओं का असर देखने को मिला।

अचानक बदले मौसम से जहां लोगों को गर्मी से कुछ राहत मिली, वहीं किसानों की चिंता बढ़ गई है। इस समय कई इलाकों में धान की खरीद और मंडियों में फसल रखने का काम चल रहा है। ऐसे में बारिश किसानों के लिए परेशानी बढ़ा सकती है।

यमुनानगर की मंडी में भीगा धान

यमुनानगर में हुई बारिश का असर मंडियों में भी देखने को मिला। मंडियों में खुले में रखी धान की फसल बारिश की चपेट में आ गई। कई जगह ट्रालियों में लदी धान की फसल भी भीग गई।

बारिश का दौर आगे भी जारी रहने की संभावना को देखते हुए किसानों और आढ़तियों की चिंता बढ़ गई है। खुले में रखी धान की फसल को बारिश से बचाना उनके लिए बड़ी चुनौती बन गया है।

12 अक्टूबर तक खराब रह सकता है मौसम

मौसम विभाग के अनुसार हरियाणा में लगातार दो पश्चिमी विक्षोभ सक्रिय हो रहे हैं। इनके प्रभाव से प्रदेश में मौसम में बदलाव का दौर जारी रह सकता है और 12 अक्टूबर तक कई क्षेत्रों में मौसम खराब रहने का अनुमान है।

बारिश का यह दौर धान की खरीद और मंडियों में खुले में रखी फसल के लिए चुनौती बन सकता है। किसानों को सलाह दी गई है कि वे अपनी फसल को बारिश से बचाने के लिए उचित इंतजाम रखें।

इन जिलों में फिलहाल मौसम साफ रहने का अनुमान

प्रदेश के कुछ जिलों में फिलहाल मौसम अपेक्षाकृत साफ रहने की संभावना है। इनमें सिरसा, हिसार, फतेहाबाद, जींद, कैथल, भिवानी, रोहतक, चरखी दादरी, झज्जर, नारनौल, रेवाड़ी, नूंह और पलवल शामिल हैं।

हालांकि पश्चिमी विक्षोभ के प्रभाव के चलते मौसम में बदलाव की संभावना बनी हुई है। इसलिए इन जिलों में भी आने वाले दिनों में मौसम की स्थिति पर नजर रखना जरूरी होगा।

किसानों के लिए बढ़ी चिंता

अक्टूबर में धान की खरीद का सीजन चल रहा है। ऐसे में अचानक बारिश होने से मंडियों में खुले में रखी फसल के भीगने का खतरा बढ़ गया है। अगर बारिश का सिलसिला जारी रहता है तो किसानों और आढ़तियों को फसल के रखरखाव के लिए अतिरिक्त सावधानी बरतनी होगी।

title: Karnataka Rainfall Deficit Raises Urban Water Risk - Urban Acres
article_text:
Karnataka rainfall deficit is no longer only a monsoon statistic. With the state recording 35% less rain than normal between June 1 and the end of September, and the India Meteorological Department forecasting below-normal rainfall during the northeast monsoon, the immediate concern is how cities and towns will manage water through a hotter and drier period.

The forecast, reported by Prajavani and attributed to the weather department, points to below-normal rainfall across much of Karnataka in October. The northeast monsoon normally begins in October and continues until the end of December, with the state expected to receive 18.2 centimetres of rain during the season. For October alone, the normal rainfall is 13.1 centimetres, but the department expects rainfall to remain below that level in most parts of the state because of the El Nino effect.

That forecast follows a monsoon that has already failed to replenish water systems evenly. Karnataka received 55.1 centimetres of rain between June 1 and the end of September, against a normal of 85.2 centimetres. The deficit for the period was 35%. In the previous month, the state recorded only 7.4 centimetres of rain against a normal of 16.1 centimetres, a shortfall of 54%.

The figures matter to urban areas because rainfall deficits accumulate across the systems that cities depend on. Reservoirs, local lakes, groundwater recharge zones and municipal supply networks are connected to seasonal rainfall, even when the impact is not visible immediately on city streets. When the monsoon underperforms and the following rainy season is also forecast to be weak, authorities face a narrower window to rebuild storage before demand rises again.

The distribution of the deficit is also significant. According to the Karnataka State Disaster Management Authority, all districts except Bengaluru South are facing severe rainfall deficiency. The report does not provide a separate explanation for Bengaluru South’s classification, but the broader state-level pattern indicates that the rainfall problem is not confined to one watershed or one urban region.

The number of taluks reporting deficient rainfall increased through the monsoon. In June, 151 taluks were facing deficient rainfall while 89 recorded normal rainfall. The number of deficient taluks rose to 174 in July, 189 in August and 228 in September. Overall, 209 taluks are reported to be facing severe rainfall deficiency, while 31 have received normal rainfall.

This progression reveals the difference between a temporary dry spell and a season-long failure of rainfall distribution. Last year, June and July also saw lower rainfall, but stronger rainfall in August helped Karnataka record above-normal rainfall overall. This year, the deficit continued from the beginning of the monsoon, leaving less opportunity for later rainfall to compensate for earlier losses.

For urban administrations, that distinction affects planning. A short dry spell can often be managed through temporary operational changes, but a cumulative deficit requires decisions about storage, allocation, groundwater use, tanker dependence and the protection of local water bodies. The report says water problems have already emerged in several parts of the state, but it does not specify the cities, reservoirs or municipal systems under greatest pressure.

The regional figures show that the deficit is spread across Karnataka’s varied landscapes. South Interior Karnataka received 21.7 centimetres against a normal 36.9 centimetres, a deficit of 41%. North Interior Karnataka recorded 27.6 centimetres against 47.9 centimetres, a deficit of 42%. Malnad received 96.5 centimetres against a normal 155.6 centimetres, a deficit of 38%. The coastal region, despite receiving the highest absolute rainfall, recorded 223.1 centimetres against a normal 310.1 centimetres, a deficit of 35%.

The data complicates the common assumption that high-rainfall regions are insulated from water stress. The coastal region received more rain than other parts of the state, but it too recorded a substantial shortfall against its normal. In practical terms, the question for water management is not only how much rain falls, but where it falls, when it falls and whether the rainfall reaches storage and recharge systems.

The district-level figures underline the uneven exposure. Mysuru recorded 17.2 centimetres against a normal 41.9 centimetres, a deficit of 59%. Vijayapura recorded 16.8 centimetres against 38.9 centimetres, a deficit of 57%. Haveri recorded a 52% deficit, while Chikkaballapur and Kalaburagi each recorded a 51% deficit. Raichur and Ballari recorded deficits of 49%, while Dharwad, Yadgir and Koppal each recorded deficits of 48%.

These locations include both growing urban centres and districts where towns depend heavily on local and regional water systems. A rainfall deficit can affect drinking-water supply, irrigation and livestock simultaneously, increasing competition between uses. Where municipal networks are weak or supply is intermittent, households and businesses may rely more heavily on private borewells, tankers or stored water. The supplied report does not quantify those effects, but the pattern of deficiency creates the conditions in which they become more likely.

The temperature forecast adds another layer to the water challenge. The weather department has warned that temperatures may rise significantly in several districts because of dry conditions. The report says maximum temperatures in many districts were already up to 5 degrees Celsius above normal during the previous month. Haveri recorded temperatures up to 6.4 degrees above normal, while maximum temperatures crossed 35 degrees Celsius in Kalaburagi, Bagalkot, Haveri and Raichur, among other districts.

Higher temperatures can increase water demand even when supply is under pressure. Urban households need more water for drinking, cooling and hygiene, while construction, commercial activity and public institutions continue to draw from municipal systems. Heat also increases the health burden on people who lack reliable indoor cooling or access to water. The source report does not provide heat-related illness figures, so the public-health impact cannot be measured from the available evidence, but the combination of heat and rainfall shortage is a clear management concern.

The institutional response will involve more than the weather department. The India Meteorological Department provides the rainfall and temperature outlook, while the Karnataka State Disaster Management Authority tracks the spread and severity of rainfall deficiency. Municipal bodies, water boards, district administrations and state departments must translate those assessments into supply decisions. Their responsibilities include monitoring available stocks, coordinating allocations and communicating restrictions or emergency measures where necessary.

The report indicates that the northeast monsoon could begin around October 16, but also says that rainfall may remain below normal in the coming days. That makes the next phase important for authorities, although the supplied material does not establish how much rainfall would be required to reverse the deficit or restore specific reservoirs and groundwater systems.

The immediate evidence confirms three linked developments: Karnataka has experienced a severe monsoon shortfall, the deficit has widened across a large number of taluks, and the next rainfall season is forecast to remain weak while temperatures rise. What remains unclear is the condition of individual urban reservoirs, the current groundwater levels, the scale of municipal supply disruption and the contingency measures being prepared by local authorities.

Those gaps are central to understanding the state’s urban water position. Rainfall data explains the pressure entering the system, but not yet how each city, town or district will absorb it. The next useful indicators will be the northeast monsoon’s actual performance, reservoir storage, groundwater conditions and official water-supply measures in the areas already reporting severe deficiency.

title: Mhadei Water Dispute: Goa Seeks Urgent Monsoon Check on Karnataka Projects - Urban Acres
article_text:
Goa Chief Minister Pramod Sawant has sought renewed action on the Mhadei water dispute, urging Karnataka’s legislative assembly Speaker G S Patil to improve relations with Goa and asking the Centre to order an immediate monsoon inspection of Karnataka’s Kalasa-Bhandura project sites.

Speaking at the Silver Jubilee celebrations of the Goa Legislative Assembly complex, Sawant said he had raised the dispute while appealing to Patil for better relations between the neighbouring states. “I urged (Karnataka speaker) to have a better neighbourly relation. When I said neighbourly relations, it includes Mhadei and I have not forgotten to mention it,” he said.

Goa and Karnataka have been engaged in the dispute for more than four decades over Karnataka’s plans to divert water from the Mhadei river through the Kalasa-Bhandura projects. The dispute has remained a major interstate water and infrastructure issue, with Goa opposing diversion plans that it says affect the river system on which the state depends.

The latest intervention comes as Goa reports that monsoon rainfall has fallen by around 32%. In a letter to the Union Ministry of Jal Shakti, the state government has asked the chairperson of Mahadayi Prawah to inspect the Kalasa and Bhandura project sites during the ongoing monsoon.

Goa wants the inspection to determine whether there have been any breaches at the project sites. It has also asked that the inspection report be submitted to the Centre and that the findings be used to recommend remedial measures.

The state’s request places particular emphasis on the physical condition of infrastructure linked to the diversion schemes. Goa has asked Mahadayi Prawah to identify and prepare an inventory of civil infrastructure constructed by Karnataka for earlier Kalasa and Bhandura diversion schemes that has become redundant or has been abandoned.

The demand follows the Central Water Commission’s technical appraisal of a revised lift diversion scheme. Goa has asked the Union ministry to take action on that appraisal, seeking either its revocation or that it be kept in abeyance.

The requests reflect the administrative layers involved in the Mhadei dispute. Political engagement between the neighbouring states is taking place alongside demands for technical inspection, regulatory review and intervention by the Union government. The Mahadayi Prawah has been identified by Goa as the body that should inspect the sites and assess the status of related civil works.

For Goa, the immediate concern is linked to both the condition of project infrastructure and water availability during a period of reduced rainfall. The state’s request for a monsoon inspection now awaits consideration by the Centre and the relevant water-management authority.

title: IMD issues yellow warnings for 3 days; western and coastal Odisha on alert - Pragativadi
article_text:
A shifting weather pattern is unfolding across Odisha as the Southwest Monsoon continues its seasonal withdrawal across eastern India.

Driven by an upper-air cyclonic circulation over southern Jharkhand and a trough line stretching from Haryana to the North Bay of Bengal, the region is bracing for severe atmospheric instability marked by thunderstorms, high winds, and fluctuating temperatures.

Rising Temperatures and Initial Rainfall Observations

In recent days, maximum daytime temperatures have surged across Odisha, climbing 3°C to 4°C above normal in several coastal areas and 2°C to 3°C above normal in interior regions. Chandbali recorded the state’s highest temperature at 36.7°C, while Bhubaneswar logged a high of 35.4°C with morning relative humidity touching 90%. Conversely, night temperatures have remained largely unchanged, dropping up to 2°C below normal in select coastal pockets.

Precipitation over the past 24 hours remained localised, with light to moderate showers hitting isolated areas in northern and central districts. Sundargarh recorded the highest rainfall at 5 cm, followed by Kamakhyanagar, Altuma, and Korei at 3 cm each.

3-Day Forecast: Yellow Warnings for Severe Thunderstorms

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) and the Regional Meteorological Centre in Bhubaneswar have issued Yellow Warnings across multiple districts over the next three days, cautioning against heavy lightning and gusty winds:

Date / Period Affected Districts Weather Alert & Wind Speeds Day 1 (Up to 08:30 IST, Oct 08) Sundargarh, Jharsuguda, Bargarh, Sambalpur Yellow Warning: Severe lightning & gusty winds (40–50 kmph) Baleshwar, Bhadrak, Jajpur, Kendrapada, Jagatsinghpur, Cuttack, Deogarh, Angul, Dhenkanal, Keonjhar, Mayurbhanj Yellow Warning: Lightning & gusty winds (30–40 kmph) Day 2 (Oct 08 – Oct 09) 12 Interior & Western Districts (Sundargarh, Jharsuguda, Sambalpur, Balangir, etc.) Yellow Warning: Widespread lightning & gusty winds (40–50 kmph) Coastal Districts (Cuttack, Jagatsinghpur, Kendrapada, Jajpur, Bhadrak, Baleshwar) Yellow Warning: Lightning & gusty winds (30–40 kmph) Day 3 (Oct 09 – Oct 10) 9 districts, including Keonjhar, Mayurbhanj, Cuttack, and Puri Yellow Warning: Thunderstorms & gusty winds (30–40 kmph)

From Day 4 onwards, active warnings are expected to subside to NIL, though light, localized rainfall will persist in southern and coastal areas. Daytime temperatures are projected to drop by 2°C to 3°C over the coming three days before stabilising.

Low-Pressure System Building in the Bay of Bengal

Adding to the atmospheric activity, renowned agricultural and meteorological expert Dr Surendranath Pashupalak noted that a low-pressure system is expected to form during the third week of the month over the North Andaman Sea and the adjoining Bay of Bengal near the Myanmar coast.

Global forecasts—including models from the US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA)—indicate a well-organised system that could bring light-to-moderate and heavy localised rainfall to coastal and southern Odisha. Experts emphasise that clarity on whether this system intensifies into a cyclone will emerge after October 15, once its trajectory and structure stabilise.

title: Odisha weather update brings soaring temperatures to Chandbali and heavy rainfall to Sundargarh - prameyanews.com
article_text:
Odisha experiences rising temperatures alongside localised heavy rainfall activity
Chandbali emerged as the hottest location in the state, recording a maximum temperature of 36.7°C, which stands 4.1°C above the normal range. Meteorological Centre Bhubaneswar released its latest Odisha weather update today, detailing clear contrasts in regional weather patterns over the past 24 hours. Nawarangpur experienced the coolest conditions, logging the lowest minimum temperature of 19.0°C. Temperature variations across different districts highlight the shifting local climate conditions.
Significant rainfall in northern districts
Sundargarh district recorded the highest rainfall amount, with the Sundergarh station receiving 52.8 mm of rain. Other areas also saw notable precipitation, including Altuma in Dhenkanal with 35.2 mm and Kamakhya Nagar with 30.2 mm. Korei in Jajpur registered 29.0 mm of rainfall, while Tangarpali in Sundargarh received 28.4 mm. Coastal and southern locations like Akhuapada in Bhadrak and Mahendragarh in Gajapati recorded lighter rainfall amounts of 12.6 mm and 12.4 mm, respectively. Historically, October weather in this region often brings varied precipitation due to withdrawing monsoon currents transitioning into the post-monsoon phase.
Twin City temperature observations
Bhubaneswar weather remained notably warm and dry during this observation period. The capital city recorded a maximum temperature of 35.4°C, which is 3.1°C higher than normal, and a minimum of 24.4°C, with no rainfall reported. Cuttack experienced very similar conditions, reaching a high of 35.0°C and a low of 27.0°C, also recording zero precipitation. Other major towns like Puri reached 36.0°C, while Daringibadi remained relatively cool at 29.5°C. Additional inland locations such as Dhenkanal and Nayagarh also reported high temperatures of 36.3°C and 36.0°C. These figures indicate an ongoing warm spell across the coastal plains following the recent monsoon season.

Gujarat Weather Updates Bhadarwa summer 2026: ગુજરાતમાં ચોમાસું આવ્યું જ ક્યારે અને કેટલું? ચોમાસું હોવા છતા તેનો અનુભવ ના થયો તેવા ઘણા વિસ્તારો છે જ્યાં લોકો સામાન્ય વરસાદનો આનંદ માણી શક્યા અને હવે વિદાય લેશે તેવા અહેવાલો મળી રહ્યા છે. ભાદરવો ચાલી રહ્યો છે ત્યારે જ એવું કહેવાય કે ભાદરવો ભરપૂર જ હોય, પણ આ વર્ષે ભાદરવો ગરમીથી ભરપૂર એવું કહેવું પડે તો પણ નવાઈ નહીં.

ગુજરાતમાં ભાદરવામાં જ્યાં કેડ સમા પાણી પણ જોવા મળતા હોય છે ત્યાં પણ હવે સુકું ભટ જોવા મળે છે. ભાદરવામાં આ વખતે છેલ્લા 24 કલાકમાં સૌરાષ્ટ્રમાં છૂટો છવાયો વરસાદ થયો પણ તે સિવાય બાકીના ભાગો મોટાભાગે સુકા રહ્યા. ભાદરવામાં મહત્તમ તાપમાનમાં 2 ડિગ્રી તાપમાન વધ્યું છે. ભૂજ અને ડીસા સૌથી ગરમ શુક્રવારે હતા. તે દિવસે 38.6 ડિગ્રી તાપમાન રહ્યું. અમદાવાદ, વડોદરા, સુરત જેવા શહેરોમાં બપોરે નીકળો તો ભાદરવામાં ચામડી દાજે તેવો તાપ જોવા મળે છે.

- Advertisement -

કેટલાક ડેટામાં પણ એવું જોવા મળી રહ્યું છે કે, આગામી 24 કલાકમાં ગુજરાતમાંથી ચોમાસું વિદાય લે તેવી સંભાવનાઓ છે. જોકે આને લઈને તમારા મનમાં એવું થાય કે ગુજરાતમાં ચોમાસું હતું જ ક્યારે? જે વિદાય લેવાનું? હવામાન વિભાગ કહે છે, આગામી 7 દિવસમાં દીવ, દમણ અને દાદરાનગર હિવેલી સહિત ગુજરાતમાંથી હવામાન સુકું રહે તેવી સંભાવનાઓ છે. આ દરમિયાન વરસાદ થાય તેવી સંભાવનાઓ નથી.

આમ પણ આ વર્ષે ચોમાસામાં 11 ટકા વરસાદ ઘટ્યો છે. ખાસ વાત કરીએ તો સૌરાષ્ટ્ર અને કચ્છમાં તો 24 ટકા વરસાદ ઓછો થયો છે. આવા સંજોગોમાં ચોમાસાની વિદાયના સમાચાર આવી રહ્યા છે, હવે આગામી એક વર્ષ રાહ જોવાની છે. આ દરમિયાન ખેડૂતો અને લોકોને કેટલી સમસ્યાઓનો સામનો કરવો પડશે તે વિચાર બહારનું છે. બીજું રાજકીય વિપક્ષો પણ દુષ્કાળ જાહેરાતની માગ કરી રહ્યા છે પરંતુ સરકાર આ વાત માનશે કે કેમ? તે પણ હજું વિચાર બહાર છે. કારણ કે દુષ્કાળ જાહેરાત માટેના કેટલા પેરામિટર્સ ફુલફિલ થાય છે તે સરકારને જ સમજવાનુ બાકી હોય તેવું લાગી રહ્યું છે.

ઉલ્લેખનીય છે કે અલ નીનોની અસર અંગે ઘણા તજજ્ઞો વાત કરી ચુક્યા છે કે તેની અસરને કારણે તાપમાન સામાન્ય કરતા વધારે રહેવાની સંભાવના છે. તો એવા સંજોગોમાં ચોમાસાની વિદાય લોકો ને ગમે તેવા સમાચાર નથી.

title: ગુજરાતમાં 6 ઓગસ્ટ સુધી ભારે વરસાદના એંધાણ, જાણો તમારા જિલ્લાની આગાહી - Mumbai Samachar
article_text:

/
gujarat

ગુજરાતમાં 6 ઓગસ્ટ સુધી ભારે વરસાદના એંધાણ, જાણો તમારા જિલ્લાની આગાહી
2026-08-01 09:02:00
Author: Mayur Patel



અમદાવાદઃ રાજ્યમાં વરસાદના ત્રીજા રાઉન્ડની ધમાકેદાર શરૂઆત થઈ છે. હવામાન વિભાગ દ્વારા 6 ઓગસ્ટ સુધીનું પૂર્વાનુમાન જાહેર કરવામાં આવ્યું હતું.  આજે હવામાન વિભાગે અમદાવાદ, આણંદ, સુરેન્દ્રનગર, રાજકોટ, બોટાદ અને ભાવનગર જિલ્લામાં વરસાદનું રેડ એલર્ટ આપ્યું છે. જ્યારે કચ્છ, અમરેલી, ભરૂચ, પાટણ, ગાંધીનગર, વાવ થરાદ, મહેસાણા, સાબરકાંઠા, મોરબી, અરવલ્લી ઓરેન્જ એલર્ટ તથા  દેવભૂમિ દ્વારકા, પોરબંદર, જામનગર, જૂનાગઢ, ખેડા, વડોદરા, સુરત, પંચમહાલ, મહીસાગર, દાહોદ, દીવ, દમણ અને દાદરા નગર હવેલીમાં યલો એલર્ટ જાહેર કરવામાં આવ્યું છે. 

આવતીકાલે કયા જિલ્લામાં પડશે ભારે વરસાદ

2 ઓગસ્ટના રોજ મોટાભાગના જિલ્લાઓમાં વરસાદનું જોર ઘટશે, પરંતુ પવનના સુસવાટા સાથે વરસાદ રહેશે. બનાસકાંઠા, પાટણ, મહેસાણા, સાબરકાંઠા, મોરબી અને કચ્છ જિલ્લામાં છૂટાછવાયા સ્થળોએ ભારે વરસાદની શક્યતા છે. ગાંધીનગર, અરવલ્લી, ખેડા, અમદાવાદ, આણંદ, પંચમહાલ, દાહોદ, મહીસાગર, વડોદરા, છોટા ઉદેપુર, નર્મદા, ભરૂચ, સુરત, ડાંગ, નવસારી, વલસાડ, તાપી, દમણ, દાદરા અને નગર હવેલી, સુરેન્દ્રનગર, રાજકોટ, જામનગર, પોરબંદર, જૂનાગઢ, અમરેલી, ભાવનગર, દેવભૂમિ દ્વારકા, ગીર સોમનાથ, બોટાદ અને દીવમાં 40 થી 50 કિમી પ્રતિ કલાકની ઝડપે ફૂંકાતા પવન અને હળવી મેઘગર્જના સાથે હળવાથી મધ્યમ વરસાદની સંભાવના છે.


3 ઓગસ્ટે રાજ્યના મોટાભાગના જિલ્લાઓમાં અમુક સ્થળોએ ગાજવીજ સાથે હળવાથી મધ્યમ વરસાદની શક્યતા છે. જ્યારે 4 થી 6 ઓગસ્ટ બનાસકાંઠા, પાટણ, મહેસાણા, સાબરકાંઠા, ગાંધીનગર, અરવલ્લી, ખેડા, અમદાવાદ, પંચમહાલ, દાહોદ, મહીસાગર, વડોદરા, છોટા ઉદેપુર, નર્મદા, ભરૂચ, સુરત, ડાંગ, નવસારી, વલસાડ, તાપી, રાજકોટ, જામનગર, પોરબંદર, જૂનાગઢ, અમરેલી, ભાવનગર, મોરબી, દ્વારકા, ગીર સોમનાથ, બોટાદ, દીવ અને કચ્છના છૂટાછવાયા વિસ્તારોમાં ગાજવીજ સાથે હળવાથી મધ્યમ વરસાદી છાંટા કે ઝાપટાં પડવાની શક્યતા છે. 


રાજ્યમાં છેલ્લા 24 કલાકમાં કેટલો વરસાદ નોંધાયો

સ્ટેટ ઈમરજન્સી ઓપરેશન સેન્ટર, ગાંધીનગર દ્વારા જાહેર કરવામાં આવેલા આંકડા મુજબ આજે સવારે 6 કલાકે પૂરા થયેલા છેલ્લા 24 કલાકમાં  255 તાલુકામાં વરસાદ પડ્યો હતો. એક તાલુકામાં 24 ઇંચથી વધારે, ત્રણ તાલુકામાં 16 ઇંચથી વધારે, ત્રણ તાલુકામાં 13 ઇંચથી વધારે, છ તાલુકામાં 10 ઇંચથી વધારે વરસાદ ખાબક્યો હતો.  

પાંચ તાલુકામાં 9 ઇંચથી વધારે, છ તાલુકામાં 8 ઇંચથી વધારે, છ તાલુકામાં 7 ઇંચથી વધારે, 12 તાલુકામાં 6 ઇંચથી વધારે, 20 તાલુકામાં 5 ઇંચથી વધારે, 11 તાલુકામાં 4 ઇંચથી વધારે,  25 તાલુકામાં 3 ઇંચથી વધારે, 48 તાલુકામાં 2 ઇંચથી વધારે,  39 તાલુકામાં 1 ઇંચથી વધારે અને 72 તાલુકામાં એક ઇંચથી વધારે વરસાદ નોંધાયો હતો. સુરતના અંબિકામાં સૌથી વધુ 24.06 ઇંચ, તાપીના ડોલવણમાં 16.73 ઇંચ, ખેડાના વસોમાં 16.38 ઇંચ, નવસારીના વાંસદામાં 16.26 ઇંચ, સુરતના ઉમરપાડામાં 14.69 ઇંચ, ખેડાના નડીયાદમાં 13.43 ઇંચ, ભરૂચના નેત્રંગમાં 13.03 ઇંચ, વલસાડના ધરમપુરમાં 11.02 ઇંચ, ડાંગના વઘાઈમાં 10.94 ઇંચ, સુરતના માંગરોળમાં 10.71 ઇંચ, આણંદમાં 10.67 ઇંચ, ડાંગના સુબીરમાં 10.24 ઇંચ, આણંદના ખંભાતમાં 10.16 ઇંચ વરસાદ ખાબક્યો હતો.

Gogoi sets midnight deadline for govt, warns of mass agitation over flood relief
The Sivasagar MLA says full compensation by October 31 would immediately end his indefinite protest against government inaction
By 
Correspondent - 7 Oct 2026 3:36 PM IST| Updated On: 2026-10-07 11:22:30

Raijor Dal chief's protest entered its sixth day on Wednesday

Guwahati, Oct 7: Raijor Dal chief and Sivasagar MLA Akhil Gogoi has threatened to intensify his indefinite sit-in at Assembly Square into a mass agitation if the Assam government fails to respond to his demands for relief and compensation for flood-affected families in Upper Assam by midnight.

Gogoi, whose protest entered its sixth day on Wednesday, said he would wait for the government’s response until midnight before deciding on the next course of action.

“If the Chief Minister does not pay heed, this protest will turn into a mass agitation. My indefinite protest will continue, and we will wait for the government’s response until midnight today. If we do not receive any response, we will intensify the protest from tomorrow,” he said.

Gogoi alleged that Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma had not given any positive response despite his week-long agitation.

He accused the Chief Minister of criticising the protest instead of addressing the concerns of flood-affected people.

The Raijor Dal chief referred to Sarma’s recent remarks that he would not support what he described as Gogoi’s attempt to “blackmail” the government.

Gogoi said the Chief Minister did not need to support his protest, but should instead support the affected families.

“You do not need to support us. You only need to support the 2 lakh people affected by the floods,” he said, adding that he would immediately withdraw the protest if the government announced full compensation for affected families by October 31.

Gogoi also questioned the government’s assessment of the number of flood-affected families in Sivasagar.

He said an assessment conducted by teachers had identified 55,000 affected families, while government data showed that 5.75 lakh people had been affected in the district.

Based on the Disaster Reporting and Information Management System (DRIMS) figures, he claimed the number of affected families would be around 1.15 lakh.

Gogoi began the indefinite sit-in on October 2 with three key demands.

These include immediate financial assistance of Rs 15,000 to Rs 25,000 for every family affected by the July 19 floods, compensation of Rs 10 lakh each for affected families and business establishments, and a CBI investigation to identify those responsible for the disaster and initiate action against them.
